data.why: The repo bundles demo microscope images (a mixed-candidate sample, a blank filter control, and a stage micrometer scale) plus a calibration.json and trained YOLOv8n weights, so the app runs fully offline with realistic inputs.

goals: Upload a microscope image of a filtered water sample and detect candidate microplastic particles (fragment, fiber, film, foam, pellet)
Check whether the optical calibration (µm/pixel scale factor) is valid, stale, or missing before trusting any quantitative size output
Run the calibration wizard against a stage micrometer image or reference polymer beads to establish/update the scale factor
Obtain calibrated particle sizes (Feret max/min, ECD) and a size-distribution histogram in micrometers
Get a per-sample confidence score and see which particles or samples are flagged for lab confirmation (e.g. FTIR/Raman)
Estimate particle concentration (particles/L) from a known filtered water volume and dilution factor, and export a JSON report

review.summary: The tree matches what Hydro Lens is for: calibrate, detect and size particles, triage them for FTIR/Raman confirmation, estimate concentration and export a report. Its phases follow the real order of work, its labels are clean, and every screen I opened shows what its node claims. It needs small fixes before filing: note that this is the legacy Streamlit UI, give the blank control its own task, demote the docs phase, and put the defects found in the run onto the features they affect.
